question: How can a redirected image be invalidated without destroying cache entries a live widget still holds?
callsite_evidence: lv_cache_drop (0x0c8b8cae) looks the entry up through the cache class (vtable +12). If the entry's reference count (entry+4) is non-zero it sets the invalidation flag at entry+12 and unlinks it through the class (vtable +20), leaving the payload allocated for the holder. Only a zero-reference entry is unlinked, passed to the payload free callback (cache+24) and then freed via 0x0c3a387a.

lv_cache_entry_release_data / lv_cache_entry_dec_ref (0x0c8b9790) decrements entry+4 and, when it reaches zero AND the invalidation flag at entry+12 is set, runs the payload free callback and frees the entry. This is the deferred-free path a retired-but-held entry takes when its last holder releases it.

By contrast the .139 LRU-rb drop_all_cb (0x0c3a7918) logs 'entry (%p) is still referenced' for held entries, skips their payload free, but then walks the red-black tree and frees every node allocation regardless of reference state.
The LRU-rb class vtable is at 0x2ca168c4; its lookup/unlink slots are 0x0c3a4ace and 0x0c3a472c respectively.
control_flow_evidence: The image cache is keyed by decoded source path, so a redirected path never reaches an image that is already cached; the entry must be retired for the redirect to be observed on the next decode.
Retiring per entry keeps the held payload valid for the current holder and guarantees the next lookup misses, so the next open of that source goes through the installed redirect.

The module walks the cache's entry list head (cache+52) and derives the lookup key from the node's payload (node -> +16), stopping if the head does not advance so a class whose unlink semantics differ cannot spin.
ownership_analysis: Retirement is a logical invalidation, not a forced release. A widget or animation that holds a decoded image keeps a valid payload until it releases its own reference; the module never frees data out from under a live holder. Must run on the UI owner thread, never under the interrupt lock.
unsafe_assumptions: No hardware execution has been performed; the .139 serial console returned no bytes on this host.

The traversal assumes the recovered LRU/RB class layout (entry list head at cache+52, payload pointer at node+0, key at payload+16) and is guarded by a class-pointer equality check against 0x2ca168c4; it must not be used for any other cache class.
Whether a widget re-opens its source on the next draw, rather than holding a decoded handle indefinitely, is NOT established by this evidence and remains per-widget.
Retirement does not reload fonts: font wrappers are page-owned and reference counted, and need the page-rebuild lifecycle.
recommended_probe: On hardware, confirm a redirected on-screen image re-decodes after retirement plus a full-screen invalidation, that a held entry's payload stays valid until its holder releases it, and that no allocator corruption or leak follows repeated activations.
